# Independent audit: outer strict approximation and finite-fiber slack

Audited `candidate ff5285005955b0c7` and
`candidate 39ba6f71d6fbae25` in full.
Both proofs pass, with the scopes stated in those notes.

## Outer approximation

1. In the ball construction the squared-radius excess over the displayed
upper bound is `2 T_k/k + (h_C(u)+1/k)^2-R^2>0`; this proves strict
containment even for negative support values. The coordinate directions
supply the claimed uniform bound, and the support-net nearest-point
argument supplies Hausdorff convergence. Finite intersections of balls
with common interior are strictly convex.
2. The finite candidate integer-base set is uniform. Empty original
fibers are eventually absent by compactness. Every nonempty original
fiber is included, and all subsequential fiber limits lie in it; this
proves slice convergence also at projection-boundary indices. Indicator
convergence is pointwise, including boundary points, because the
approximation is outer. Thus the nonnegative measure difference has
mass exactly `M_k-M`, with no section-boundary exception.
3. The uniform normalized-depth estimate follows with denominator
`M_k`, as written. Upper semicontinuity of closed-halfspace depth uses
parallel outward enlargement, so positive boundary mass presents no
problem. One convergent sequence of centers gives one limiting center
valid for all halfspaces.
4. For `d=1`, strict convexity leaves endpoint `H_0` mass one; the note
correctly does not claim a facet-null approximation in that dimension.
For `d=0`, the support eventually stabilizes exactly.
5. The intrinsic diagonal first thickens only continuously, hence keeps
the exact original integer projection. Choosing the outer error relative
to each positive tube mass gives convergence of normalized measures.
For each closed enlarged halfspace, Portmanteau has the needed direction:
`limsup nu_j(H_delta)<=nu(H_delta)`. Since every sufficiently late mass is
at least the target constant, the limit has that lower bound. Sending
`delta` down to zero retains every closed halfspace, including intrinsic
boundary mass. This is conditional transfer of a depth theorem, not a
proof of its premise.

## Compatibility slack

1. Removing the target coefficient is essential and is done explicitly.
Every remaining base representation uses at least two distinct points;
strict ambient convexity puts its entire compact Minkowski interpolant
strictly inside the target fiber. In particular a zero-volume target
has no such representation.
2. It suffices to take the minimum slack at the finitely many vertices
of the representation polytope: the Minkowski-distributivity equality
used to extend it holds because every source set is convex. This gives
a single positive inward distance at every constrained target.
3. A Hausdorff perturbation by less than epsilon moves every weighted
interpolant by at most epsilon. The support-function description proves
`K_z eroded by epsilon B` is contained in the perturbed target. Taking
`2 epsilon<delta_z` proves all required inclusions. Reinstating the
removed target coefficient is then ordinary convexity.
4. `conv(P) intersect Z^n=P` follows using ALL nonempty original fibers,
not only the positive-volume indices. Thus no missing zero fiber or new
integer fiber is overlooked.
5. If the base affine span is deficient, perpendicular thickening fixes
all slices at bases in that span exactly. Restricting first to, say,
`eta<=1` gives a finite candidate lattice list; then choosing eta below
the positive perpendicular distances excludes all other bases. The
original full continuous fiber and spanning base differences give the
required relative dimension, and perpendicular thickening makes the
realization ambient full dimensional.

No strict-class minimum attainment, uniform slack along a sequence, or
quantitative depth bound is inferred from either result.
